why: Bench test of the bump alone (not for a check): the wall with self 4 and neighbours 2, bias -3, and a run drive R held on (bias 8, +3 to every node), against a global inhibitor G (reads the wall's sum x 1, bias -4, -6 to every node). Calculated: the run drive lifts all nodes until noise ignites a few; neighbour excitation favours a contiguous group, and G grows with the sum and holds the rest down. To see at each light level whether a bump of 2-6 nodes forms, how hard it pulls, and whether its direction holds over 30 ticks.
